OrganizationSettings.description:
Organization-level configuration and facts about the org's licensing and infrastructure.

Attributes:
    gitleaks_license_owned: Whether the organization owns a gitleaks commercial license.
        Determines whether to use the gitleaks GitHub Action (requires license)
        or the license-free Docker image path for secret scanning. Set once at the org
        level; gate-drain and other periodic runs consult this config rather than
        asking the operator per-decision.

gitleaks_license_owned.description: Whether the organization owns a gitleaks commercial license. When true, the gitleaks GitHub Action can be used for secret scanning; when false, use the license-free Docker image path instead.
gitleaks_license_owned.title: Gitleaks License Owned

OrganizationSettings.title: OrganizationSettings

CentralDeploySettings.description:
Central-deploy roster and component-access settings.

Provides the base URL for the central-deploy management-plane API.
At session start the agent fetches the
``GET /chat/components`` roster (a list of component agents the chat
is allowed to call), caches it with a short TTL, and loads each
component's declared skill into the agent.

Attributes:
    url: Canonical base URL of the central-deploy / deploy-lifecycle API
        (no trailing slash).  Single source of truth for the deploy-plane
        address; the lifecycle client and feedback roster lookup both read
        it (the former ``lifecycle.base_url`` was retired in favour of it).
    roster_cache_ttl: Seconds to cache the roster before re-fetching.
        Default 300 (5 min).
    component_response_max_chars: Maximum characters of a component API
        response returned to the agent; longer bodies are truncated.
        Default 200000.
    deploy_api_key: Canonical deploy-plane credential — the shared
        secret between this chat component and central-deploy.  Sent as
        the ``X-API-Key`` header on outbound roster/lifecycle calls, and
        required (matched) on inbound central-deploy → chat endpoints
        (``/chat/github/*`` and the feedback roster lookup).  This is the
        single source of truth; the per-block ``deploy_api_key`` fields
        were retired in favour of it.
    component_credentials: Per-component credentials keyed by
        component id.  Each entry carries credentials for all
        supported auth schemes; the roster entry's ``auth.type``
        selects which fields are used.

component_request_timeout.description: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds) for component API calls made via component_request.  Also bounds the total wall-clock time for all retry attempts via the retry deadline.  Default 60s — raise this if upstream components are slow to respond.
component_request_timeout.title: Component Request Timeout

component_fallbacks.description: Baked-in fallback base URLs for components that may be missing from the central-deploy roster (e.g. after a redeploy). Keyed by component id (e.g. "robotsix-mill"). When the roster returned by central-deploy is missing a component, the fallback URL is used instead. This keeps monitors running through transient roster gaps.
component_fallbacks.title: Component Fallbacks

CentralDeploySettings.title: CentralDeploySettings

ComponentClientSettings.description:
Component agent client settings — inspect and configure remote agents.

When enabled, the chat agent gains four tools: ``list_component_agents``,
``get_component_telemetry``, ``get_component_config``, and
``set_component_config`` so it can enumerate configured component agents,
read live telemetry, and read/update configuration on demand via direct
HTTP.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds).
    components: Allowlist of component agents the chat may contact.
        Each entry has a ``base_url`` and an optional ``label``.
ComponentClientSettings.title: ComponentClientSettings

ComponentCredentials.description:
Stored credentials for a single roster component.

Keys are component IDs matching the ``id`` field returned by the
central-deploy ``GET /chat/components`` roster. Each entry carries
credentials for all supported auth schemes; the roster entry's ``auth.type``
selects which fields are used.

Attributes:
    basic_auth_username: Username for HTTP Basic authentication.
    basic_auth_password: Password for HTTP Basic authentication.
    header_token: Token value for header-based authentication
        (e.g. ``X-API-Key``).
ComponentCredentials.title: ComponentCredentials

ComponentTarget.description:
Network address and optional label of a component agent.

Attributes:
    base_url: HTTPS base URL of the component (e.g.
        ``https://internal.service:8000``).
    label: Optional human-readable label for display (e.g. "robot-brain").
ComponentTarget.title: ComponentTarget

ConversationSettings.description:
Conversation persistence and memory settings.

Attributes:
    persist_path: Path to the JSON file where conversations are written.
ConversationSettings.title: ConversationSettings

ContinuationSettings.description:
Continuation (post-restart auto-resume) settings.

When a session is interrupted mid-turn, the continuation system
automatically resumes it on the next server boot. This block controls
the maximum number of restarts a single session may experience before
it is archived and no longer auto-resumed.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch. When ``False`` continuation is disabled
        — interrupted sessions are not resumed.  Default ``False``
        (continuation is feature-gated and must be opt-in).
    max_consecutive: Maximum number of consecutive (back-to-back) restarts
        a session may experience before it is archived and no longer
        auto-resumed. Default 3 — a session that restarts 3 times in a
        row without completing a turn is assumed to be broken and is
        closed. Set to a higher value if the server is expected to restart
        frequently.
ContinuationSettings.title: ContinuationSettings

DiagnosticsSettings.description:
Automated problem detection (diagnostics), recurring-issue clustering, and fix proposals.

The diagnostics system monitors the board for patterns in ticket state
transitions: a ticket that transitions to ``errored`` (implement crashed),
``fixing_ci`` (pre-existing CI failures), or other error states triggers
a diagnostic event. The system clusters recurring issues (same repo, same
error pattern), proposes fixes via a dedicated model, and surfaces them
for validation.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch. When ``False`` diagnostics are not collected.
    store_path: Path to the JSONL diagnostic events store.
    proposals_path: Path to the JSON proposals archive.
    effectiveness_path: Path to the JSON effectiveness reports archive.
    recurrence_threshold: Minimum count of matching events within the
        recurrence window before an issue is considered recurring and a
        fix proposal is emitted. Default 3 (an issue that repeats 3 times
        is recurring).
    recurrence_window_days: Time window (days) in which the recurrence
        threshold must be reached. Default 30 — a recurring issue is one
        that matches 3+ times within the last 30 days.
    observation_window_days: Time window (days) for the recent-activity
        window when analyzing recurring issues and proposing fixes.
        Default 30 — the proposal considers tickets and changes from the
        last 30 days.
    mill_events_path: Path to the mill component's diagnostic event log
        (read-only; symlinked from central-deploy's mill data directory).
DiagnosticsSettings.title: DiagnosticsSettings

DockerDigestSettings.description:
Docker Registry v2 digest-resolution tool.

When enabled, the agent gains a `resolve_docker_digest` tool that
queries the Docker Registry v2 HTTP API to resolve a Docker image
reference (e.g. ``python:3.14-slim``, ``ghcr.io/owner/image:tag``) to
its immutable `sha256:...` content digest.
DockerDigestSettings.title: DockerDigestSettings

DirectRepoSettings.description:
Lightweight direct-PR path for simple, low-risk changes.

When enabled, the chat agent gains tools to create branches, commit
changes, and open pull requests in one call — without requiring a mill
ticket in BLOCKED state. The opened PR is the review gate: a human
approves and merges it, so this path stays safe and reversible.

Four secrets (GitHub App credentials) are required for this to work.
They must be stored securely via the environment variable setup script
(not pasted into chat). The install instructions live in the
robotsx-standards documentation.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False`` the direct-repo tools are
        not offered.
    direct_fix_enabled: Sub-switch for the `direct_fix` escape-hatch tool
        (push commits directly to target branch, bypassing PR). This is a
        last-resort tool for unblocking mechanically simple, validated-correct
        fixes; leave it ``False`` unless explicitly activated by an operator.
    github_app_id: GitHub App ID (numeric, from the app settings page).
    github_app_private_key: GitHub App private key (PEM format, from the
        app settings page).  **Do not paste into chat** — load from
        environment via the setup script.
    github_app_installation_id: GitHub App installation id on the target
        org. Obtained by following the 'Install now' link on the app
        settings page.
    github_api_base_url: GitHub API base URL (typically
        ``https://api.github.com`` for GH.com, or an on-prem URL for
        GitHub Enterprise). Default ``https://api.github.com``.
    board_api_base_url: Mill board API base URL. Default
        ``http://127.0.0.1:8077`` (localhost, served by this same process).
    board_api_token: HTTP Bearer token for mill-board authentication
        (optional; localhost access is unauthenticated).
DirectRepoSettings.title: DirectRepoSettings

EvergoingSettings.description:
Long-running conversation auto-trim settings.

When a conversation is very long, the agent automatically compacts its
own outputs to free up context for new replies. This block controls how
the trim is executed.

Attributes:
    trim_interval_seconds: Minimum elapsed seconds before another trim is
        considered. Default 1800 (30 minutes) — the trim will not run again
        until 30 minutes have passed since the previous trim.
    keep_recent_runs: How many recent agent runs (typically subsession
        completions) to preserve in the compacted transcript. Runs older than
        this are consolidated into a prose summary. Default 5 — keep the 5
        most recent runs verbatim, summarise everything before that.
EvergoingSettings.title: EvergoingSettings

FeedbackSettings.description:
Automated chat-session feedback loop — surfaces actionable findings from session transcripts.

The feedback system runs in the background (on a schedule or
on-demand) and analyzes closed chat sessions to surface actionable
improvements: mis-routed decisions, overly-conservative prompts,
inconsistent tool use, and other issues that repeat across sessions.

Attribute
    enabled: Master switch. When ``False`` the feedback loop is disabled.
    model_level: Model tier to use for feedback analysis (1, 2, 3).
        Default 1 (cheap, extractive model); raise to 2 or 3 for more
        sophisticated analysis.
    board_url: Base URL of the mill board API (where feedback findings are
        filed as tickets). Default empty string (use the ``mill`` component
        from central-deploy roster).
    board_api_token: HTTP Bearer token for mill-board authentication
        (optional; localhost access is unauthenticated).
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout for board API calls (seconds).
        Default 60.
    max_tickets_per_run: Maximum number of finding tickets to file in a
        single feedback run. Default 3 (file at most 3 tickets). Set to 0
        to disable filing (feedback analysis will still run, but findings
        will not be filed as tickets).
    dedup_window_seconds: Time window (seconds) in which duplicate findings
        are deduplicated. A finding that matches a recent finding (same
        category, same repo, same title) within this window is dropped.
        Default 60 — check the last 60 seconds of the ticket store for
        duplicates.
    ingest_max_retries: Maximum retry attempts when filing a finding ticket
        via the mill's ingest endpoint. Default 2.
    max_concurrent_runs: Maximum number of feedback analysis runs that can
        execute concurrently. Default 2 — analyze at most 2 sessions in
        parallel.
FeedbackSettings.title: FeedbackSettings

FileHubToolsSettings.description:
File-hub tools — document fetch, fill, render, and upload.

The file-hub component stores, converts, and serves various document
formats (PDF, images, etc). This block configures the agent's connection
to it.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    base_url: URL to the file-hub component (default
        ``http://file-hub:8080``).
    working_dir: Local filesystem directory where files are downloaded
        during form-fill and conversion workflows. Temporary files are
        stored here; the directory is not persisted across restarts.
    max_download_bytes: Maximum size (bytes) of a single file download.
        Default 52,428,800 (50 MB).
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds).
FileHubToolsSettings.title: FileHubToolsSettings

GatewayRouteSettings.description:
Gateway route tool — query DNS and gateway status for deployed services.

The robotsix fleet uses a single DNS entry with a gateway domain
(e.g. ``deploy.robotsix.net``), under which multiple services run
(chat, mail, invest, etc.) at subdomains. This tool enables queries
to the gateway's status and route table.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds).
    gateway_base_domain: Gateway base domain (e.g.
        ``deploy.robotsix.net``). Routes to individual services are
        constructed as ``<service>.<gateway_base_domain>``.
GatewayRouteSettings.title: GatewayRouteSettings

GitHubActionsSettings.description:
GitHub Actions — create or update a repository Actions secret via the GitHub App installation.

When enabled, the chat agent gains an ``set_actions_secret`` tool that can
create or update a GitHub Actions secret in a repository. The secret value
is encrypted with the repo's public key before transmission — the server
never retains the plaintext.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False``, no Actions secret tool
        is offered.
    github_org: GitHub organisation name whose repos are in scope
        (e.g. ``"damien-robotsix"``).  The tool only targets repos
        under this org.
GitHubActionsSettings.title: GitHubActionsSettings

GitHubSecuritySettings.description:
Repository security-feature toggle via the GitHub App installation.

When enabled, the chat agent gains a ``set_repo_security_and_analysis``
tool that can enable or disable repository-level security features
(dependency graph, advanced security, secret scanning) on repos under
the configured GitHub App's installation scope.

**Guardrails built into the tool (not configurable):**
- Repo scope is resolved dynamically from the GitHub App installation
  (list-installation-repositories) — no static allowlist.
- Only repos within the installation scope are modifiable.
- Each feature toggle explicitly requires ``"enabled"`` or ``"disabled"``
  — no accidental bulk changes.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False``, no security-feature tool
        is offered.
    github_org: GitHub organisation name whose repos are in scope
        (e.g. ``"damien-robotsix"``).  The tool only targets repos
        under this org.

The inbound ``X-API-Key`` presented on the
``PATCH /chat/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/settings`` endpoint is matched
against the canonical ``central_deploy.deploy_api_key`` (the per-block
``deploy_api_key`` was retired).  When that key is empty, the endpoint
returns 503 (unconfigured).

Note: GitHub App authentication is delegated to
:class:`DirectRepoSettings` — those credentials must also be configured
for the tool to function.
GitHubSecuritySettings.title: GitHubSecuritySettings

HealthSettings.description:
Server health check and liveness probe settings.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False`` health endpoints are disabled.
    path: HTTP path for the health check endpoint (default ``/health``).
HealthSettings.title: HealthSettings

HttpProbeSettings.description:
HTTP Probe — read-only uptime and render-probe tool.

When enabled, the agent gains an `http_probe` tool that performs a
single HTTPS GET against a public URL, follows redirects (up to the
configured limit), and returns a structured health report. This is
read-only — no state mutation.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    timeout: HTTP read timeout (seconds). Default 10.
    allowlist: List of hostnames that http_probe may target.  When empty,
        all hostnames are allowed (no restrictions).
    max_body_bytes: Maximum response body size to download and return.
        Larger bodies are truncated with a note. Default 2048 (2 KB).
    max_redirects: Maximum number of redirects to follow (default 5).
        Chains longer than this are truncated with a note.
HttpProbeSettings.title: HttpProbeSettings

KnowledgeSettings.description:
Long-term knowledge base settings.

The knowledge base is a per-agent store of operational facts and
findings that an agent author creates and updates manually. Unlike
automatic conversation memory (which is similarity-recalled), the
knowledge base supports explicit authorship and lookup by id.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False`` the knowledge base
        is disabled.
    path: Path to the JSON file where knowledge notes are stored.
KnowledgeSettings.title: KnowledgeSettings

LangfuseSettings.description:
LLM observability and tracing (Langfuse).

Langfuse is a data pipeline that observes and records all LLM
calls (prompts, responses, costs, latency) made by the agent and its
subsessions. The logs are critical to debugging and cost accounting.
This block configures the Langfuse connection and per-project routing.

Attributes:
    host: Langfuse deployment host URL (e.g. ``https://cloud.langfuse.com``,
        or an on-prem URL). Default ``https://cloud.langfuse.com``.
    projects: Per-project Langfuse configuration keyed by ``<repo_id>``
        (e.g., ``"robotsix-chat"``, ``"robotsix-mail"``, etc). Each entry
        carries a ``public_key`` and ``secret_key`` pair. When a subsession
        is spawned for a repo, it uses the Langfuse credentials from the
        matching ``projects`` entry (default empty — subsession observability
        uses the default public/secret key pair).
LangfuseSettings.title: LangfuseSettings

LangfuseInspectSettings.description:
Trace inspection tool — read-only query of Langfuse observability data.

When enabled, the agent gains an ``inspect_langfuse_trace`` tool that
queries the Langfuse API to fetch and summarize recent traces.
Primarily used to diagnose implement-stage failures by inspecting the
agent's own LLM-call traces linked to a specific ticket or run.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    max_traces: Maximum number of traces to fetch and summarize in a
        single call. Default 5.
LangfuseInspectSettings.title: LangfuseInspectSettings

LangfuseProjectSettings.description: Per-project Langfuse credentials (public key, secret key).
LangfuseProjectSettings.title: LangfuseProjectSettings

LifecycleSettings.description:
Central-deploy lifecycle API integration.

The lifecycle API (served by central-deploy) manages the robotsix Docker
fleet: service status, environment variables, restarts, and deployments.
This block configures the agent's connection to it.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False`` lifecycle tools are not
        offered.
    default_protocol: HTTP protocol to use for lifecycle service URLs
        (typically ``http`` for localhost or behind a reverse proxy).
        Default ``http``.
    api_key: Authentication token for lifecycle API calls.
        (Must match the ``DEPLOY_API_KEY`` env var on central-deploy.)
    service_name: The name of this service as it appears in the
        central-deploy service registry (e.g. ``chat``, ``mail``, …).
        Used for self-restart operations.
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds).
    self_restart_max_retries: Maximum number of restarts to attempt
        before giving up. Default 3.
LifecycleSettings.title: LifecycleSettings

MemoryComponentSettings.description:
Robotsix memory component integration (long-term fleet memory).

The robotsix-memory component stores durable facts, preferences, and
outcomes across agents and sessions. This block configures integration
with the memory component.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch. When ``False`` memory component integration
        is disabled.
    base_url: HTTP base URL of the memory component (default
        ``http://memory:8080``).
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds). Default 30.
    allow_override: Whether agents may override previously-stored
        facts. Default ``True`` — an agent may overwrite an existing
        memory entry. Set to ``False`` to pin values and prevent changes.
MemoryComponentSettings.title: MemoryComponentSettings

OpenrouterSettings.description:
OpenRouter API integration (LLM routing and fallback).

OpenRouter is a unified API that routes LLM requests across multiple
backends (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) with per-key and per-model fallback
handling. This block configures the OpenRouter integration.

Attributes:
    api_key: Canonical OpenRouter API key. Default empty string
        (unconfigured).
    keys: Named API keys for per-project routing. Keyed by project
        (e.g. ``"robotsix-chat-cognee"``, a model fine-tune). When the
        agent uses a model with a project name, it looks up the key
        in this map and uses that key; otherwise it falls back to the
        canonical ``api_key``.
OpenrouterSettings.title: OpenrouterSettings

PeriodicSessionSettings.description:
Configuration for a single periodic subsession.

Attributes:
    name: Unique name for this periodic session (e.g., ``"gate-drain"``,
        ``"dependabot-drain"``). Used as the subsession label and to
        reference the session in commands.
    initial_prompt: The initial system prompt / instructions for the
        periodic agent. This is the agent's complete specification —
        what to do, what tools to use, what to report, and any
        constraints.
    schedule_interval_seconds: How often (in seconds) to spawn a new
        run of this periodic session. Default 3600 (hourly). Set to 0
        to disable scheduling (manual trigger only via the
        ``POST /periodic/definitions/{name}/run`` endpoint).
    anchor_utc: Optional RFC-3339 timestamp in UTC (e.g.
        ``"2026-09-07T06:00:00Z"``) that anchors the schedule. When set,
        the first run is scheduled for this time; subsequent runs follow
        the interval. This is useful for synchronizing periodic runs with
        a specific time of day.
    model_level: LLM model tier for this agent (1, 2, 3).
        Default inherits the subsession default (usually 2). 1 is
        cheap/fast for routine checks; 2 is the workhorse tier; 3 is
        frontier reasoning.
    enabled: Whether this periodic session is active (can be spawned).
        Default ``False`` (must be explicitly enabled).
PeriodicSessionSettings.title: PeriodicSessionSettings

PeriodicSettings.description:
Periodic (background) subsessions — tasks that repeat on a schedule.

Periodic sessions allow the operator to define long-running subsessions
that repeat on a schedule (e.g., hourly, daily). Each session is a
self-contained agent task with its own initial prompt, model tier, and
schedule. Common use cases include gate-drain, dependency-update triage,
and CI monitoring.

Attributes:
    ready_staleness_minutes: Threshold (minutes) before a ticket in
        ``ready`` state is considered stale and should be prioritized
        for work. Default 10 minutes.
    priority_ready_staleness_minutes: Threshold (minutes) before a
        priority ticket in ``ready`` state is considered stale.
        Default 60 minutes.
    sessions: List of periodic session definitions.
PeriodicSettings.title: PeriodicSettings

PublicFetchSettings.description:
Public URL fetch tool — read-only web browsing with rate limits.

When enabled, the agent gains a `public_fetch` tool that performs
HTTP GET against URLs on an allowlist of domains. Useful for browsing
public resources (documentation, status pages, API responses) without
leaving the chat runtime. This is read-only — no state mutation.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    timeout: HTTP read timeout (seconds). Default 10.
    max_body_bytes: Maximum response body size to download. Larger
        bodies are truncated with a note. Default 1 MB.
    max_redirects: Maximum number of HTTP redirects to follow.
        Default 5.
    domain_allowlist: List of domain hostnames that public_fetch may
        contact. When empty, all public domains are allowed (no
        restrictions). When non-empty, ONLY these domains may be
        contacted (e.g., ``["github.com", "status.github.com"]``).
    rate_limit_requests: Maximum number of requests in the rate-limit
        window. Default 10.
    rate_limit_window_seconds: Time window for rate-limit counting.
        Default 60 seconds.
PublicFetchSettings.title: PublicFetchSettings

RefdocsSettings.description:
Reference documentation tool — read-only lookup of markdown docs from git repos.

When enabled, the agent gains a `read_reference_doc` tool that fetches
and returns the contents of markdown documentation files from registered
git repositories. Useful for looking up architecture docs, API contracts,
and other reference materials without the full repo context.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch. When ``False``, no reference-doc tool
        is offered.
    repos: Allowlist of ``{repo, ref}`` entries. Each entry specifies
a registered GitHub repository and a git ref (branch, tag, or
        commit SHA) to use. When a lookup is requested, the tool is
        restricted to these repos and refs; arbitrary repos cannot be
        queried.
    ref: Default git ref to fetch when a lookup does not specify one
        (default ``main``).
    base_url: GitHub API base URL (typically
        ``https://api.github.com`` for GH.com, or an on-prem URL for
        GitHub Enterprise).
    timeout: Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds).
RefdocsSettings.title: RefdocsSettings

RenderUrlSettings.description:
Render URL — headless Chromium page capture.

When enabled, the agent gains a `render_url` tool that loads a URL in
a headless Chromium browser, captures a full-page screenshot, and
extracts the ARIA accessibility tree. Useful for seeing how a page
renders (vs. raw HTML), finding visual issues, and reading text from
complex layouts. This is read-only — no clicks, no form fills, no
state mutation.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    timeout: Browser load timeout (seconds). Default 30.
    viewport_width: Browser viewport width (pixels). Default 1280.
    viewport_height: Browser viewport height (pixels). Default 720.
RenderUrlSettings.title: RenderUrlSettings

RepoStudySettings.description:
Repository study tool — fetch and analyze code for a bounded scope.

When enabled, the agent gains a `fetch_repo_for_study` tool that
clones a git repository into a temporary workspace, lists and reads
files, and performs regex searches — all within a bounded time (TTL)
and size envelope. Useful for large-scale code analysis, migrations,
and architectural decisions without the overhead of direct repository
operations.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    data_dir: Base directory where repo workspaces are extracted.
        Default ``/data/repo_study``.
    ttl_minutes: How long (minutes) a repo workspace remains available
        after last access before being cleaned up. Default 240 (4 hours).
    max_archive_bytes: Maximum size (bytes) of a cloned repository
        (before extraction). Large repos are rejected. Default 64 MB.
    max_extracted_bytes: Maximum total size (bytes) of extracted files
        across all workspaces. When exceeded, older workspaces are
        evicted. Default 256 MB.
    max_read_bytes: Maximum file size (bytes) that can be read in a
        single `read_repo_file` call. Default 200 KB.
RepoStudySettings.title: RepoStudySettings

SelfReviewSettings.description:
Self-review and introspection tool — agent analyzes its own recent activity.

When enabled, the agent gains a `read_recent_activity` tool that lists
its own recent actions (file edits, tool calls, transitions) and summaries
for self-review and introspection. Useful for answering questions like
"what have I done recently?", "what is still pending?", or
"have I completed this task?".

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.
    recent_activity_limit: Maximum number of recent items to return
        in a single `read_recent_activity` call. Default 20.
SelfReviewSettings.title: SelfReviewSettings

SftpSettings.description: SFTP client tool — remote file transfer via SSH/SFTP.
SftpSettings.title: SftpSettings

VersionCheckSettings.description: Version-check tool — monitor for upstream changes (e.g. release tags).
VersionCheckSettings.title: VersionCheckSettings

VolumeToolsSettings.description:
Volume tools — local filesystem directory listing.

When enabled, the agent gains a `list_volume_files` tool that lists
the contents of directories under the configured volume root (typically
``/data``). This is a read-only discovery tool — no state mutation, no
file read or write.  Useful for discovering available files and
resources without guessing individual file paths.

Attributes:
    enabled: Master switch.  When ``False`` volume tools are not
        offered.
    root_path: Root directory path to list from (default ``/data``).
VolumeToolsSettings.title: VolumeToolsSettings

vision_model.description: OpenRouter model id used to caption attached images when the active chat model lacks vision support. Empty string means 'vision model unconfigured', which triggers the curated no-image-support failure path.
vision_model.title: Vision Model
